openings.claim: Replace manual per-batch amendment lookup with an auditable directed revision register containing only explicit amendment-to-superseded-row edges. Usefulness under missing links is uncertain. No conversion/revision coupling is proposed.
openings.discriminator: Against manual reconciliation checking amendment references and retaining all rows, the register may reduce unsupported definite claims when replacements appear under another identifier or references disappear. Compare supported resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims, and requests naming missing records. Equal results with greater register effort defeat its claimed advantage; improvement is not assumed.
openings.probe: Use the supplied script or spreadsheet: prepare both variants in 35 minutes, run each on both supplied copies in 20, and freeze all four output sets by minute 60. Each covers twelve batches with quantities or bounded disagreements, citations, and at most three targeted requests naming missing fields or records. Never silently drop duplicate or unmatched rows; use only the supplied conversion table; never infer from neighboring batches. Flag the disturbed missing superseded reference and undefined status; request identities or definitions when indispensable. Compare frozen outputs with the sealed key during the supplied extra twenty minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Matching quantities or earlier effective times do not prove the differently identified older-report row is the same replacement. Missing cross-report identity evidence can prevent resolution. Cycles, conflicting replacements, or absent referenced rows defeat a unique replacement conclusion. Never invent undefined status semantics: ambiguous rows remain visible, cited, and bounded. Register construction and four outputs must fit sixty minutes; allocation is unmeasured and the cap proves no feasibility. If preparation overruns, stop without extension, record the incomplete probe, and claim no success. No deployment or reliable performance is established.
